test_title: PYST 43: RRB Group D - Mathematics (Held On: 16 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: maths
question: A hole can empty a full tank in 1 hour. To maintain the level of water in the tank, 3 filling pipes of equal efficiency are required. How many more such filling pipes are required so that an empty tank gets filled in 3 hours?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Hole empties = 1 tank/hr ⇒ 3 pipes balance it ⇒ 1 pipe = 1/3 tank/hr

Required net fill rate for 3 hours = 1/3 tank/hr

Let total pipes = n ⇒ net rate = n/3 − 1

n/3 − 1 = 1/3 ⇒ n = 4

**∴ Answer = 1 more pipe**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Hole empties tank in 1 hour, 3 pipes maintain level

**Formula used:**

Work = Efficiency × Time

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let total work = 1 tank

⇒ Emptying rate (hole) = 1 tank/hr

⇒ 3 pipes balance it ⇒ total filling rate = 1 tank/hr

⇒ So, 1 pipe fills = 1/3 tank/hr

⇒ Let required number of pipes = n

⇒ Net filling rate = n × (1/3) − 1

⇒ Tank must be filled in 3 hours ⇒ rate = 1/3 tank/hr

⇒ n/3 − 1 = 1/3

⇒ n/3 = 4/3

⇒ n = 4

⇒ Extra pipes required = 4 − 3 = 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1 more pipe.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns Concept

Filling is positive work and emptying is negative work

Efficiency

Efficiency = Work done per unit time

Balancing Condition

If level remains same ⇒ filling rate = emptying rate

Net Work

Net rate = Filling rate − Emptying rate
